4 اترّ ; (T, S, M, A, K;) and ↓ تَرَّ , (IDrd, M, K,) inf. n. تَرٌّ; (IDrd, M;) or the former only; (M;) He cut off (T, S, M, K) a man's arm, or hand, by a blow, or stroke, (T, S, M, A,) of a sword; (T, S, A;) made it to fall off: (S:) and in like manner, any member: (M:) as also اطرّ and اطنّ. (T.) ―
-b2- And the former, (S, A, TA,) or ↓ the latter, (M, as in the TT,) He (a boy) made the piece of wood called قُلَة to fly away [by striking it] with the مِقْلَآء. (T, S, * M, * A, * TA.) ―
-b3- اترّهُ قَوْمُهُ His people separated him from themselves. (As, T.) ―
-b4- اترّهُ القَضَآءُ Fate drove him far away from his country, or town. (S, M, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
